Distribution & biogeography of Consorophylax species. The genus Consorophylax has a strictly European alpine distribution. Most species are restricted to small areas, like C. carinthiacus Malicky 1992 (Karnische Alpen, southern Alps), C. corvo Malicky 2008 (Piemont, western Alps), C. delmastroi Malicky 2004 (Piemont, western Alps), C. montivagus (McLachlan 1867) (Koralpe, Saualpe, southeastern Alps), C. piemontanus (Piemont, western Alps) (Fig. 2). Consorophylax styriacus Botosaneanu (in Kimmins & Botosaneanu 1967) (eastern Alps) and C. consors (McLachlan 1880) (western Alps) have a slightly broader distribution within the Alpine arc (Fig. 2). Although we do not know the exact distribution range, C. vinconi sp. nov. is possibly another microendemic species within the genus. Consorophylax vinconi sp. nov. is most similar to C. piemontanus, which was described from Avigliana, some 13 km west of Torino. Interestingly, the type locality of C. vinconi sp. nov. is about 56 km north-northeast from the type locality of C. piemontanus. This supports the interpretation of C. vinconi sp. nov. as an alpine microendemic.
